questions.q: What is a runbook, per this lesson?
options: A written, specific reference mapping known incident symptoms to concrete diagnostic and response steps
A general knowledge test given to new DBAs
An automated script that resolves all incidents without human involvement
A log of every query run against production in the last 24 hours
questions.explain: A runbook gives specific 'if X, check Y, then do this' guidance rather than requiring general knowledge to be applied fresh under pressure.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say a runbook's value isn't about teaching something new?
options: It removes the need to think clearly under pressure at 2am, which is genuinely harder than thinking clearly during normal hours
Runbooks are only useful for training new hires, never during real incidents
Runbooks replace the need for any diagnostic scripts
Runbooks are automatically generated by SQL Server
questions.explain: The runbook's leverage comes from reducing improvisation under fatigue and pressure, not from introducing new information.

questions.q: What are the two conditions this lesson uses to decide whether something is paging-worthy?
options: It must be both urgent (needs attention now) and actionable (there's something the on-call person can do about it right now)
It must involve data loss and cost more than a set dollar amount
It must have occurred at least three times before
It must be reported by a customer directly
questions.explain: The lesson's threshold requires both urgency and actionability — an urgent but non-actionable issue, or a low-urgency issue, isn't necessarily paging-worthy.

questions.q: What is the risk of setting the paging threshold too sensitive, per this lesson?
options: On-call becomes exhausting noise and people learn to ignore pages
SQL Server automatically disables paging after too many alerts
It has no real downside since more alerts are always better
It causes tempdb to fill up faster
questions.explain: Over-paging burns people out and teaches them to tune out alerts — the same failure mode as treating every incident as maximum severity.

questions.q: Why does a pre-built diagnostic toolkit matter for on-call, per this lesson?
options: It lets a DBA go from being paged to looking at the actual problem quickly, instead of writing and debugging T-SQL from memory half-awake
It automatically fixes any incident without DBA involvement
It eliminates the need for a runbook entirely
It is only useful during business hours, not overnight
questions.explain: Tested, ready-to-run scripts for common checks (blocking, waits, tempdb usage, log_reuse_wait_desc) save critical time exactly when clear thinking is hardest.
